detail.longDescription: Web-based AI interfaces like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are fantastic for brainstorming, but completely cut off from your local repository files. To bridge this securely, TokenCap implements a local HTTP daemon via tokencap serve adhering to Bridge Contract v1. Security Architecture of the Bridge Loopback Binding: The daemon listens exclusively on 127.0.0.1:4545 . It never binds to 0.0.0.0 or public network adapters. Ephemeral Token Auth: When starting, a random hex token is generated and stored locally in ~/.tokencap/ . Requests must provide this token via the X-TokenCap-Token header. Strict Origin Checks: Pre-flight CORS filters block unauthorized web domains. Only approved extension origins can read responses. Running in the Terminal # Start in the foreground tokencap serve # Or run as a detached background daemon tokencap serve --daemon # Stop the daemon tokencap serve --stop Console Output: TokenCap bridge on 127.0.0.1:4545 Pair the companion: 127.0.0.1:4545/?pair=8f1c3a09e… Bridge context pre-warmed in 280ms. Serving intelligence for: /Users/dev/repos/api-backend Because the bridge pre-warms intelligence in memory, subsequent context generation queries take milliseconds.
